title: Vantage Point Ventures v. Sterling Commercial Properties: HVAC Compliance Dispute
premise: A startup office tenant disputes a commercial lease termination where the landlord alleges 'structural instability' due to unpermitted HVAC modifications that the tenant claims were necessary for compliant air quality standards.

side_A.role: an organiser with a tenants' union
side_A.goal: supporting the tenant against an unfair eviction

side_B.goal: justifying the eviction on grounds of lease violations

=== DOCUMENT 1: Lease Agreement and Related Correspondence (Excerpts) ===

**AGREEMENT OF LEASE**
**Date:** March 15, 2023
**Landlord:** Sterling Commercial Properties
**Tenant:** Vantage Point Ventures
**Premises:** Suite 402, 1400 Meridian Ave

**Section 12.4: Alterations and Structural Modifications**
Tenant shall not make any structural modifications to the Premises without the prior written approval of Landlord. Any such approval shall be at the sole discretion of Landlord. Tenant acknowledges that the Premises are part of a larger commercial structure constructed in 1998, and that unauthorized modifications may compromise the integrity of shared systems.

**Section 18.2: Termination and Restoration**
Upon termination of this Lease for any cause, Tenant shall be responsible for all costs associated with the removal and restoration of any modifications made by Tenant to the Premises, returning the space to its original condition, less ordinary wear and tear.

**Section 22.1: Rent and Utilities**
Base Rent is set at $4,500.00 per month for the initial five (5) year term. Tenant shall pay all utility charges for the Premises directly to the applicable service providers.

**CORRESPONDENCE LOG**

**From:** Vantage Point Ventures (legal@vantagepoint.com)
**To:** Sterling Commercial Properties (management@sterlingcommercial.com)
**Date:** August 2, 2023
**Subject:** Request for Approval: HVAC Ducting Modification, Suite 402

Dear Management,

Pursuant to Section 12.4 of our lease, we hereby submit this written request for your approval to modify the existing HVAC ducting in Suite 402. The proposed work involves the installation of a new air handling unit in the ceiling plenum to address internal air circulation issues. We request your written approval within the timeframe mandated by local commercial tenancy regulations.

Sincerely,
Vantage Point Ventures

**Status Note:** No response received from Sterling Commercial Properties within the 10-business-day response period mandated by local commercial tenancy regulations. The deadline for response expired on August 14, 2023.

**From:** Vantage Point Ventures (legal@vantagepoint.com)
**To:** Sterling Commercial Properties (management@sterlingcommercial.com)
**Date:** March 5, 2024
**Subject:** Response to Notice of Lease Termination; Request for Waiver

Dear Management,

We are in receipt of your Notice of Lease Termination dated February 28, 2024, which cites a "material breach of Section 12.4" and "structural instability." We firmly dispute these claims.

First, regarding authorization: Under local commercial tenancy law, if a landlord fails to respond to a modification request within 10 business days, the request is deemed approved by default. Our request was submitted on August 2, 2023, and you failed to respond by August 14, 2023. Therefore, the modification was legally authorized.

Second, regarding necessity: The modification was not an aesthetic upgrade but a necessary compliance measure. Pre-modification air quality testing indicated levels that violated OSHA guidelines for indoor air quality in office spaces. The local OSHA guideline recommends a maximum PM2.5 concentration of 12 µg/m³ for 8-hour workdays. Our initial sensors recorded an average PM2.5 level of 18.5 µg/m³, which is a clear violation. We had no choice but to rectify this to ensure a safe working environment.

Third, regarding structural integrity: We have obtained an independent engineering assessment which confirms the installation is within load capacities.

We request that you waive the cure requirement and rescind the termination notice.

Sincerely,
Vantage Point Ventures

**From:** Sterling Commercial Properties (management@sterlingcommercial.com)
**To:** Vantage Point Ventures (legal@vantagepoint.com)
**Date:** February 28, 2024
**Subject:** NOTICE OF LEASE TERMINATION

Dear Tenant,

This letter serves as formal notice of termination of the Lease Agreement for Suite 402 at 1400 Meridian Ave, effective March 29, 2024.

Grounds for termination include:
1. Material breach of Section 12.4 (Unauthorized Structural Modifications).
2. Structural instability resulting from unauthorized HVAC modifications.

You are hereby granted a 30-day cure period, expiring on March 29, 2024, to remedy the breaches. Failure to cure will result in eviction proceedings.

Sincerely,
Sterling Commercial Properties

=== DOCUMENT 2: Incident and Maintenance Log ===

**STANDBY MAINTENANCE LOG – STERLING COMMERCIAL PROPERTIES**
**Building:** 1400 Meridian Ave
**System:** Central Chiller and HVAC Distribution

**Entry ID:** 2024-01-12-004
**Date:** January 12, 2024
**Time:** 09:15 AM
**Technician:** G. Miller, Facility Director
**Location:** Mechanical Room, B1 / Suite 402 Plenum (Remote Monitoring)

**Observation:**
During routine quarterly inspection of the central chiller system, anomalous load patterns were detected. The primary chiller unit (Unit C-1) is operating at higher capacity than projected for this season.

**Analysis:**
Cross-referencing with tenant modification records, it was noted that Suite 402 (Vantage Point Ventures) installed a new air handling unit in September 2023. The internal maintenance report notes that the HVAC modifications in Suite 402 have increased the load on the main building's central chiller system.

**Data Points:**
- Pre-Modification Baseline (Summer 2023): Chiller Efficiency 85%
- Current Reading (Jan 2024): Chiller Efficiency 72%
- Energy Consumption Delta: +15% attributed to Suite 402 draw during peak hours.

**Action Taken:**
Flagged for engineering review. No immediate shutoff performed due to tenant occupancy.

**Entry ID:** 2023-09-05-002

**Time:** 10:30 AM

=== DOCUMENT 3: Independent Inspection Report ===

**STRUCTURAL ENGINEERING INSPECTION REPORT**
**Client:** Sterling Commercial Properties
**Project:** 1400 Meridian Ave, Suite 402
**Inspector:** Robert Vance, Senior Engineer, Sterling Commercial Properties
**Date of Inspection:** April 10, 2024
**Report Date:** April 12, 2024

**1. Purpose of Inspection**
This report was commissioned following the Notice of Lease Termination issued on February 28, 2024. The purpose was to assess the structural integrity of the ceiling plenum in Suite 402 and determine if the installation of the new air handling unit has compromised the safety of the building.

**2. Methodology**
Visual inspection of the ceiling grid, review of original architectural drawings (1998), and calculation of static and dynamic loads imposed by the new equipment.

**3. Findings**
The inspection confirmed that the weight of the new air handling unit was within the static load capacity of the existing ceiling grid, provided the unit was mounted to the main structural beams.

However, further analysis reveals concerns regarding dynamic loads. The HVAC modification introduced dynamic loads during operation that exceeded the design parameters of the ceiling grid. The vibration frequencies generated by the fan motor are resonating with the existing support structure.

**4. Conclusion**
While the static weight is acceptable, the dynamic forces create a latent structural instability. This instability poses a safety risk to the building, particularly to the ceiling tiles and lighting fixtures directly above the unit. The current configuration is not compliant with safety standards for commercial tenancy.

**5. Recommendations**
Immediate removal of the air handling unit or retrofitting of the ceiling grid with additional bracing to accommodate the dynamic loads.

**Signed:**
Robert Vance
Senior Engineer
Sterling Commercial Properties

**APPENDIX A: Contrasting Engineering Assessment (Submitted by Tenant)**
*Note: The following is a summary of the report submitted by Vantage Point Ventures, prepared by Sarah Jenkins, Structural Engineer.*

**Summary of Sarah Jenkins’ Report (March 25, 2024):**
"The ceiling grid in Suite 402 was designed with a 25% safety margin. Our calculations indicate that the installation of the air handling unit did not exceed the static load capacity, thereby negating any claim of structural instability. The dynamic loads are negligible and well within the damping capacity of the existing grid materials. No safety risk exists."

=== DOCUMENT 4: Witness Statements ===

**STATEMENT OF DR. ELENA ROSTOVA**
**Role:** Indoor Air Quality Expert for Vantage Point Ventures
**Date:** April 15, 2024

I have been retained by Vantage Point Ventures to assess the air quality conditions in Suite 402. My findings are unequivocal. The pre-modification PM2.5 levels of 18.5 µg/m³ violated OSHA guidelines, making the HVAC modification a legally necessary action to ensure a safe working environment for employees.

I installed three independent air quality sensors in Suite 402 on August 20, 2023, prior to the HVAC modification. These sensors recorded an average PM2.5 level of 18.5 µg/m³. The local Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) guideline for indoor air quality in office spaces recommends a maximum PM2.5 concentration of 12 µg/m³ for 8-hour workdays. Any level above this is a compliance violation. It was not a choice; it was a necessity.

After the HVAC modification, the air quality sensors in Suite 402 recorded an average PM2.5 level of 9.2 µg/m³ over the subsequent 30 days. This confirms that the new system is functioning correctly and has brought the space into compliance. The tenant acted responsibly to protect their staff.

**STATEMENT OF MARCUS THORNE**
**Role:** Building Manager for Sterling Commercial Properties
**Date:** April 15, 2024

I am the Building Manager for 1400 Meridian Ave. I have managed this building for twelve years. The pre-modification air quality was within acceptable commercial standards, and the modification was an unnecessary aesthetic upgrade requested by the tenant to accommodate personal preferences, not a compliance requirement.

The tenant’s claim of a "compliance violation" is a fabrication. The sensors they installed were likely miscalibrated or placed in areas with poor ventilation, skewing the data. The building has 15 other commercial units in the Meridian Ave building, none of which have reported similar HVAC-related structural issues or air quality complaints since the building was constructed in 1998. If the air were truly toxic, we would have seen complaints from other tenants or regulatory flags long before Vantage Point moved in. They simply wanted a "better" airflow for their own comfort, and they bypassed the proper approval process, which is a breach of contract regardless of the air quality narrative.

**STATEMENT OF LIAM O'CONNOR**
**Role:** Legal Counsel for Vantage Point Ventures
**Date:** April 16, 2024

I represent Vantage Point Ventures in this dispute. The core of this case is the authorization of the modification. Under local commercial tenancy law, the landlord's failure to respond to the written request within 10 business days constitutes a legal deemed approval, making the modification authorized.

Sterling Commercial Properties received our request on August 2, 2023. They had 10 business days to respond. They did not respond by August 14, 2023. The law is clear. The specific contractual term in the lease does not override the statutory requirement for a response period. By their inaction, Sterling waived their right to deny the request. The modification was legally valid from the moment the response period lapsed. Their attempt to terminate the lease based on "unauthorized" work is legally baseless.

**STATEMENT OF DIANA KOWALSKI**
**Role:** General Counsel for Sterling Commercial Properties
**Date:** April 16, 2024

I am the General Counsel for Sterling Commercial Properties. I reject the tenant's legal argument regarding "deemed approval." The lease explicitly requires written approval for structural modifications, and the general law regarding deemed approval does not override the specific contractual terms agreed upon by both parties.

Contract law prioritizes the specific terms of the agreement over general statutory defaults when the parties have expressly agreed to a different process. Section 12.4 of the lease states that approval is at the "sole discretion" of the Landlord and requires "written approval." The tenant cannot unilaterally interpret their silence as consent. The tenant proceeded with work without our written permission, which is a clear material breach. The "deemed approval" clause in local law applies to standard maintenance requests, not major structural modifications that affect the building's integrity.

**STATEMENT OF TOMMY REED**
**Role:** HVAC Technician for Vantage Point Ventures
**Date:** April 17, 2024

I performed the installation of the air handling unit in September 2023. I was present for the initial setup and the subsequent monitoring. The internal maintenance report from Sterling was based on faulty sensor calibration, and independent testing shows the central chiller system operated within normal efficiency parameters after the modification.

Sterling’s claim that our unit caused a 15% increase in energy consumption is nonsense. Their central chiller system was already aging and inefficient. When we installed our unit, we did so according to code. The load on the chiller is standard for an office of this size. In fact, our unit reduced the load on the old ductwork by providing localized conditioning. I have seen Sterling’s data, and it is misleading. They are blaming our equipment for their own poor maintenance of the central plant.

**STATEMENT OF GRACE MILLER**
**Role:** Facility Director for Sterling Commercial Properties
**Date:** April 17, 2024

I have been the Facility Director for 1400 Meridian Ave for eight years. I oversee all mechanical systems. The HVAC modification caused a 15% increase in energy consumption for the central chiller system, resulting in increased operational costs for the landlord and reduced efficiency for other tenants.

We do not make up numbers. Our monitoring systems are calibrated annually. The data is clear: before September 2023, our chiller efficiency was stable. After the installation in Suite 402, the draw increased significantly. The tenant’s unit is pulling excessive static pressure from the shared trunk line, forcing the central chiller to work harder to maintain pressure for the other 14 tenants. This is a direct financial and operational impact on the building. The tenant is aware of this and has ignored our requests to rectify it. This is not about air quality; it is about one tenant exploiting shared building infrastructure for their own benefit at the expense of the other tenants.
